author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the confusion isn't the problem, but the expectation that you must choose? In this deeply personal TEDx talk, Iris Muche explores bisexual invisibility, belonging, and why embracing life's spectrum is more powerful than fitting into a binary. 

https://www.irismuche.com  

Iris Muche is a psychosocial counsellor, trainer, and author. In 2021, she launched the blog "Die Max Mustermann" to inspire people to stop living their lives as placeholders waiting for something to happen, but rather to live self-determined lives guided by their own values. True to the motto: because your normal matters too! 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why being bisexual made me feel invisible | Iris Muche | TEDxDonauinsel Salon

description: Racism isn't always depicted by blatant beliefs, thoughts, and actions. It is often found in subtle mannerisms and deeds that may be considered commonplace. West has always been a staunch supporter and advocate of peace and respect for all people by actively increasing awareness and celebration of all people as a Minister, Mediator and conflict resolution specialist, a Life Coach and Divorce Coach. She holds a BS in Human Services Management and a MA in Christian Ministry and is a TEDx ThirdWard speaker. She also serves as a Women’s Pastor and is a member of several organizations promoting peace and civil rights. She is the proud mother of three adult children and a doting grandmother. description:
In mapping and analyzing issues at work that impact media workers' mental health and well-being, a paradoxical conclusion emerges: what makes media work special is also what can make its people sick. Drawing on his research Mark Deuze explores the challenges of living a good life in media. 
 Mark Deuze is Professor of Media Studies at the University of Amsterdam, author of 14 books (including "Life in Media" with The MIT Press), and bass player of the band Skinflower. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: Byron Adams examines how people understand and negotiate who they are across cultures, particularly in contexts of inclusion and marginalization, with the aim of translating research into more inclusive organizations and societies. Byron G. Adams is an Assistant Professor in Psychology at the University of Amsterdam, the Netherlands, and a Senior Research Associate in the Department of Industrial Psychology and People Management at the University of Johannesburg, South Africa. He is an identity psychologist whose work examines how people understand and negotiate who they are across cultures, particularly in contexts of inclusion and marginalization, with the aim of translating research into more inclusive organizations and societies. description: Drawing on her award winning research, Joyeeta Gupta proposes the development of a global constitution. Through her talk she outlines her vision for a novel multilateral agreement that seeks to address the pressing challenges of today. Joyeeta Gupta is Professor of Environment and Development in the Global South at the University of Amsterdam and Professor at IHE-Delft Institute for Water Education. She received much of prestigious academic recognition, such as the Spinoza prize in 2023 (the highest academic recognition in the Netherlans), the Amsterdam Impact Prize in 2025 and the 2022 Piers Sellers Prize for climate research. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Weber Martins parte de sua trajetória de quase quatro décadas estudando Inteligência Artificial para discutir os efeitos da rápida disseminação das IAs generativas, especialmente sobre crianças, adolescentes e a educação. Segundo sua argumentação, vivemos uma era de “falsa síntese”, na qual sistemas conseguem produzir textos e conteúdos sofisticados sem necessariamente representar compreensão. No ambiente educacional, o risco surge quando o estudante obtém resultados aparentemente excelentes sem realizar o esforço cognitivo necessário à aprendizagem. Weber contesta, nesse sentido, a expressão “dívida cognitiva”: para ele, determinadas perdas devem ser compreendidas como dano cognitivo, pois etapas importantes do desenvolvimento e da aprendizagem podem não ser plenamente recuperáveis posteriormente. A situação é agravada pelo aumento do tempo de tela, pela crescente mediação tecnológica das relações e pelo uso da IA até mesmo como fonte de apoio afetivo.

title: Inteligência Artificial: um meio para evoluir a inteligência humana | Weber Martins | TEDxGoiânia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores what makes a city not only competitive, but human. Drawing on
interviews with investment promotion agencies and economic development
organizations, it reflects on how investors and decision-makers from different
nationalities look beyond infrastructure, technology, and business conditions to ask a
deeper question: can people feel safe, welcomed, connected, and able to build a life
here? At its heart, this is a talk about future cities that are smart, sustainable, and
deeply human.

 Alia El Banna is a Professor of Marketing at Porto Business School, co-director of the International MBA, and an entrepreneur. Her research examines how places are represented and experienced, and how these representations shape the decisions and behaviours of residents, tourists, investors, and skilled workers. She focuses on place brand co-creation, authentic place narratives, the factors influencing place-related decisions, and the role of media in crafting compelling stories about pl
title: What makes a city human? | Alia El Banna | TEDxPortoSalon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A talk parte de uma tensão deliberada: quando falamos de smart cities, a maioria das pessoas pensa imediatamente em tecnologia: sensores, dados, plataformas, inteligência artificial. A proposta é desafiar essa ideia, mostrando que a cidade verdadeiramente inteligente não é a que tem mais tecnologia, mas a que coloca as pessoas no centro de cada decisão.

 Foi Vice-Presidente e Vereador da Câmara Municipal do Porto, responsável pelos pelouros do Ambiente e Transição Climática e da Inovação e Transição Digital, entre 2013 e 2025. Presidiu aos Conselhos de Administração da Porto Ambiente e da Águas e Energia do Porto, da Agência de Energia do Porto e da Associação Porto Digital, e integrou o Conselho de Administração da LIPOR. Foi Vice-Presidente da Energy Cities e membro do Grupo Consultivo de Presidentes de Câmara da Missão Europeia para 100 cidades inteligentes e climaticamente neutras. Presidiu ao Fórum do Ambiente da EUROCITIES entre 2018 e 2023, após ter sido Vice-Presidente. Ao lo
title: A cidade inteligente não se vê | Filipe Araújo | TEDxPortoSalon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Os esports já não são o futuro - são uma indústria global que já está a acontecer. Da alta performance à tecnologia, da propriedade intelectual à formação de talento, os esports estão a desafiar a forma como entendemos o desporto. E talvez sejam também um laboratório para percebermos como será o entretenimento e o trabalho do futuro.

 Pedro Almeida Couto é co-fundador da RELUPE (agência de investigação lusófona em esports) e membro do corpo editorial da RBDE. É ex Diretor de Educação e Investigação Científica na Federação Portuguesa de Desportos Eletrónicos e Diretor de Operações da Betclic Apogee Esports, doutorado em Gestão pela Universidade de Milão e do Porto e orientador de alunos de Doutoramento e Mestrado. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A tecnologia está quase tão humana como nós! Quanto mais tecnológicos nos tornamos, mais antropomórfica é a tecnologia. O que vai acontecer a seguir? O que vai acontecer às pessoas, e às relações, e à sociedade? Na verdade, não sabemos! O que sabemos é que há três necessidades emocionais básicas fundamentais para o seu funcionamento e que não nos parece que irão desaparecer em breve: conexão, pertença e propósito. 
Nesta talk a Ana Isabel explora cenários em que estas necessidades são satisfeitas pela tecnologia e não pelas relações com outras pessoas. 

 A Ana Isabel é psicóloga clínica e da educação. Com larga experiência em contextos de intervenção clínico, escolar e corporativo.  Ao longo do seu percurso tem aprofundado o estudo da comunicação humana e das competências emocionais, procurando compreender a forma como influenciam o bem-estar, as relações e o desenvolvimento de cada pessoa. Atualmente é diretora clínica da Winmotional. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TE
title: Porque não devemos humanizar a tecnologia! | Ana Isabel Lage Ferreira | TEDxPortoSalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Your career isn’t broken; the system is, and you’re allowed to redesign your life strategically instead of blaming yourself for not fitting a rigged game. Rafael Tsantes is a Glasgow-based designer and learning technologist who grew up in Athens, trained in theatre, retrained into communication design at the Glasgow School of Art, and built a career in the creative industries without financial backing or traditional entry routes. He now runs a purpose-led design studio focused on mission-driven organisations. His talk pushes back against the polished success narratives that dominate creative and tech industries - arguing that for people without safety nets, career-building isn't a heroic journey. It's a survival design problem. Rafael makes the case that "failure" is not the opposite of success - it's a signal about power, privilege, and access, and that design thinking is not a creative luxury but a political tool for navigating systems that were never built for everyone. Part person
title: Survival Design | Rafael Tsantes | TEDxLeith

author: TEDx Talks
description: The introduction of genetically engineered seeds in the mid-1990s fundamentally changed the economics of American farming. It locked farmers into a razor-and-blade business model of patented seeds and proprietary chemicals, exploded farm debt to a record $600 billion, and created the conditions for the largest corporate agricultural acquisition in history. This is the story of a former Wall Street analyst turned whistleblower and activist who called out a $63 billion acquisition made without a shareholder vote. She argues we can't change the food system by auditing our shopping carts alone. We must also examine the systemic financial levers that determine how we direct capital, demand transparency, and allocate subsidies. Robyn O'Brien is a former Wall Street food industry analyst turned whistleblower, who became one of the first major voices to connect the introduction of genetically engineered crops and glyphosate-based herbicides to the rise of food allergies, childhood cancers, an
title: What would it take to fundamentally change the American food system? | Robyn O'Brien | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
角　潤一 : 人を惹きつける「オーラ」を放つ人間になるために、できること

学生の頃から、人々を惹きつける「オーラ」を放つ人間になりたいと思っていた彼は、
長年、日本の外交官として、紛争地帯や国連代表部など、世界各地で働いてきた。
多くの要人たちと出会い、彼らと自分は何が違うのかを考える中で彼が見つけた、
「オーラ」を放つ人間に共通するもの、そしてそうなるために、何ができるのか。

SUMI Junichi : How to Develop an Aura That Draws People In

Since his student days, he has dreamed of becoming someone who radiates an aura that naturally attracts and inspires others.
Over the years, he has served as a Japanese diplomat, working in conflict zones, at the Permanent Mission to the United Nations, and in diverse parts of the world.
Through encounters with world leaders, diplomats, and influential figures, he began to wonder: What sets people with a powerful aura apart from everyone else?
In this talk, he explores the qualities they share and reveals the habits and mindset that anyone can cultivate to develop an aura of their own.


 “A Persian-speaking diplomat, made in Okinoshima, from the Land of Eight Million Gods.”
Born in Omori, Iwami Ginzan World Heritage site, raised in Izu
title: 人を惹きつける「オーラ」を放つ人間になるために、できること | Junichi SUMI | TEDxKumamoto

author: TEDx Talks
description: Symbols of morality are often cheaper than responsibility. Opening with China's sky-high bride price, where a ritual of respect can quietly stand in for the conditions of actual respect, this talk follows a single pattern through performative wokeness, its anti-woke reflection, nationalism that leans on borrowed glory, and even the debate over whether mahjong is heritage or gambling. Drawing on a friendship that unravelled over these very questions and on the classical ideal of "unifying knowledge and action", it argues that the real opposite of moral performance is responsibility, and leaves the audience with one uncomfortable question: are we trying to understand, to repair, or simply to look good? Ziyue Frank Huang is a multilingual student, writer, musician, activist, and professional mahjong player whose work moves across politics, philosophy, language, and art. He self-identifies as liberal, yet his political convictions are shaped by an intense inner conflict: a refusal to mist
title: Is It Wokeness, Compassion, Hypocrisy, or Egotism? | Ziyue Huang | TEDxGCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: This TEDx talk reveals a harsh truth: your zip code predicts your health better than your genes. Starting with a map of Baltimore showing opioid overdose deaths concentrated in West Baltimore (21217), the speaker argues that the deadliest “pathogen” has no DNA—it lives in policies, environments, and unequal opportunities. Using the fictional story of Maria, she explains three mechanisms: environmental deprivation, toxic stress that rewires biology, and the erosion of hope. The call to action: the next great health breakthroughs must come not just from labs, but from urban planning, economic policy, and restoring dignity. Health should not be predetermined by where you are born. Huangchuye, a young observer and thinker from China who is passionate about social justice and public health. He is deeply fascinated by the hidden systems that shape human destiny, particularly the realization that a person's well-being is often determined by their postal code long before birth. He believes th
title: Why Your Zip Code is a Better Health Predictor Than Your Genes | Chuye Huang | TEDxGCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if ancient myths could help us understand modern emotions? Through the stories of Yu the Great, Nüwa, and Jingwei, this talk explores how Eastern myths can give shape to feelings that are difficult to put into words, including pressure, self-doubt, and the emotional weight behind constant effort. Instead of treating myths as distant moral lessons, the talk presents them as an emotional language that can help us better understand what is happening inside us. Selina Lu is a high school student whose work explores the connection between mythology, psychology, and teenage emotional experience. Her independent research, Deconstructing and Reshaping “Archetypes”: How Chinese Mythological IP Character Design Fosters Critical Cultural Identity in Adolescents, examines how mythological figures can shape the way young people understand identity and culture. Building on this interest, she created a healing handbook that uses Eastern myths as symbolic tools for understanding pressure, self-d
title: When Emotions Are Too Complex: Healing Through Eastern Myths | Yuetong Lu | TEDxGCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Under the watchful gaze of society, individuals often polish a flawless "mirror" to present to the world, leaving our true selves buried within imperfect echoes. Journeying across time and space – from the melancholic cadence of Nanyin blind storytelling ballads to the unrestrained release of karaoke nights – this talk examines how embracing the power of our "masks" allows us to rediscover authentic human resonance beneath the surface of external perception. Olivia Shen is a cultural researcher and community organiser dedicated to social inclusion. As the lead of accessibility initiatives for visually and hearing-challenged communities, she works to build practical bridges of empathy and communication. Olivia's research focuses on the intersection of identity and performance, specifically hothrough the academic study of Naamyam – an ancient Cantonese narrative singing tradition historically performed by blind storytellers. By investigating how these historical performers used characte
title: Mirrors and Echoes: The Reality Behind Perception | Olivia Shen | TEDxGCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the person you become is shaped by what you do in the next five seconds? We often imagine that character is built through big decisions and defining moments. But student speaker Rhea Joseph  offers a different perspective: who we become is often shaped by the small choices that happen so quickly that we barely notice them. From choosing whether to include someone who is standing alone to deciding whether to laugh at a cruel joke, help someone, or own up to a mistake, these moments may seem insignificant. But together, they compound. Every small decision becomes a vote for the person we are becoming. Drawing from psychology, neuroscience and her own experience, Rhea explores why the brief gap between an impulse and an action can be so important, particularly during our teenage years. That pause gives us an opportunity to step back, question our instinct and choose how we want to respond. Her central question is simple but powerful: Which version of me do I want these next five
title: How Five Seconds Can Change You | Rhea Joseph | TEDxWisdom World School Amanora

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How does social media shape the way young people see themselves?

In a world where likes, comments, followers, views, and online approval can influence how we feel about ourselves, our digital lives are increasingly becoming part of our identity. For today’s digital natives, social media is not simply a platform for communication—it can shape self-image, confidence, belonging, comparison, and self-worth.

This talk explores the psychology of digital identity and the impact of online validation on young people’s emotional well-being. It examines why we seek approval in digital spaces, how social comparison affects self-esteem, and what happens when our online identity begins to influence how we understand our real-world identity.

Drawing on psychological research and insights from digital well-being, education, and youth development, the talk offers practical, evidence-based strategies for developing a healthier relationship with social media and technology.

title: The Psychology of Digital Identity | Sapphire Shakya | TEDxXavier International School Youth
